Lekhraj And Another" (Jt 1999 (9) Sc ... on 17 October, 2022 In The Court Of Ms. Nabeela Wali Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate-01 New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts: New Delhi In the matter of : Cc No. :- 42902/2016 Food Inspector Department of Pfa Govt of Nct of Delhi A-20 Lawrence Road Industrial Area Delhi-110035 .... Complainant Versus 1. Sh. Ravi Kumar S/o Sh. Raj Kumar M/s Baniya General Store, Shop No. 315, Main Bazar, Subzi Mandi, Delhi-110007 R/o 366, Gali Robin Cinema Subzi Mandi, Delhi-110007 ... Vendor
texts.facts: The present complaint has been filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as PFA Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. 2. As per the complaint, on 20.06.2009 at about 02:45 PM, Food Inspector (herein after referred to as 'FI') Sh. Sanjeev Kumar Gupta, visited the premises of M/s Baniya General Store, Shop No. 315, Main Bazar, Subzi Mandi, Delhi-110007 and purchased a sample of Ghee for food analysis from Sh. Ravi Kumar where the said food article was found stored for sale. The sample consisting of approx. 750 gms of Ghee was taken from an open aluminium tub having no label declaration. Vide report dated 06.07.2009, the public analyst reported that the sample was substandard because BR exceeds State Of H.P. vs . Lekhraj And Another" (Jt 1999 (9) Sc ... on 17 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135532912/ 2 the prescribed maximum limit of 43 and Reichert value is less than the minimum limit of 28. It also gives a positive B T test which should be negative in ghee. Subsequently on the basis of the report, the present complaint was filed. 3. Since the complaint was filed by a public servant in writing, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and NABEELA WALI WALI Date: 2022.10.17 17:09:50 +0530 CC No:- 42902/2016 DA (FSO) v. Ravi Kumar Etc. Page No. 3 of 19 the accused was summoned vide order dated 23.11.2019. 4. On appearing before the Court, accused persons were admitted to bail and provided with copy of complaint. Pre-charge evidence was recorded and subsequently vide order dated 12.05.2010 charge under Section 16(1) (a) of PFA Act 1954 and Section 16(1)(c) r/w Section 7 of the PFA Act was framed upon both accused persons, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. COMPLAINANT EVIDENCE 5. At the trial, the complainant department i.e. the prosecution examined three witnesses in support of its case. 6. Sh Sanjiv Kumar Gupta, Food Inspector was examined as PW- 1. PW-1 in his examination-in-chief stated that on 20.06.2009 he had visited the shop of the accused where accused Ravi Kumar was found conducting the business of sale of 'Ghee'. As per PW-1 after disclosing his identity, he purchased 750 grams of ghee from an open aluminum tub having no label declaration, after properly mixing with the help of clean and dry measure and rotating in all possible directions. As per PW-1 he paid Rs.135/- vide vendors receipt Ex.PW1/A as sample price. After lifting of sample, it was divided into three parts as per NABEELA NABEELA WALI WALI Date: 2022.10.17 17:09:58 +0530 CC No:- 42902/2016 DA (FSO) v. Ravi Kumar Etc. Page No. 4 of 19 procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules and separately packed and sealed in clean and dry glass bottles. As deposed by PW-1, vendor signatures were obtained on the LHA slip. As per PW-1 one counter part of the sample was deposited with the public analyst (PA) on the next day and remaining two counterparts were deposited with the LHA. PW-1 further deposed that on receipt of the PA report Ex PW1/G the sample was found not-conforming to standards as BR exceeded the prescribed maximum limit of 43 and Reichert value is less than the minimum limit of 28. BT test was positive. PW-1 further deposed that he further investigated the matter and sent a letter ExPW1/H to STO Ward No. 40 to disclose the constitution of M/s Baniya General Store and as per its reply at portion A, no such firm was found registered with the Sales Tax. During investigation, Sh. Raj Kumar was found proprietor of the said shop and Sh. Ravi Kumar was the vendor. PW-1 further deposed that after completion of investigation, the complete case file along with all the statutory documents were sent to the Director Shri D.P. Dwived through SDM/LHA. As per the witness after obtaining due sanction of the Director, PFA the present complaint was filed against the accused persons. PW-1 exhibited the following documents i.e. State Of H.P. vs . Lekhraj And Another" (Jt 1999 (9) Sc ... on 17 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135532912/ K : Intimation letter along with PA reprot; 12. Ex. PW1 / L : Copy of postal registration receipts. 13. Mark X : Photocopy of ration card. 7. PW-1 was duly cross-examined by counsel for accused and denied the suggestions put to him. 8. Sh. R.K. Sharma, SDM/LHA, who was part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings was examined as PW-2. PW-2 deposed on similar lines as PW-1 and identified his signatures on relevant documents. He deposed that during sample proceedings he tried to associate customers, passers-by and neighbours but none came forward and hence FA Sh. Mittar Pal was joined as a witness. Digitally signed by NABEELA NABEELA WALI WALI Date: 2022.10.17 17:10:13 +0530 CC No:- 42902/2016 DA (FSO) v. Ravi Kumar Etc. Page No. 6 of 19 9. PW-2 was cross examined by counsel for the accused and deposed that he was not having any knowledge about the accused persons, prior to lifting of the sample. The witness was confronted with copy of order of a Writ Petition filed before Hon'ble Delhi High Court which is Mark D-1 and later exhibited as Ex.PW2/D-1 and copy of Action Taken Report which is Mark D-2. He further deposed that he was not aware regarding any order dated 08.08.2007, passed by Hon'ble Delhi High Court, copy of which is Mark D-3. 10. Sh. Mittar Pal, Retd. FA, was examined as PW-3. PW-3 deposed about joining the proceedings with PW-1 and PW-2 on 20.06.2009. He further deposed that before starting the sample proceedings, Fl requested some passersby and neighbouring shopkeepers to join as a witness in State Of H.P. vs . Lekhraj And Another" (Jt 1999 (9) Sc ... on 17 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135532912/ 4 sample proceedings, but none came forward and hence on the request of PW-1 he joined the sample proceedings PW-3 deposed that PW-1 had purchased 600 grams of ghee from the accused. As deposed by PW-3 the accused had also produced a pamphlet which is Ex.PW1/A1 wherein rate of commodities sold at his shop was mentioned. The witness identified his signature at point A on Ex.PW1/D1. 11. PW-3 was duly cross-examined by counsel for accused wherein he stated that no site plan was prepared in the present case. PW- 3 was also cross- examined on the location of the shop of the Digitally signed by NABEELA NABEELA WALI WALI Date: 2022.10.17 17:10:38 +0530 CC No:- 42902/2016 DA (FSO) v. Ravi Kumar Etc. Page No. 7 of 19 accused, by the defence counsel. No other witness was examined and complainant's evidence was then closed. EXAMINATION OF ACCUSED U/S 313/281 CRPC 12. Thereafter, all the incriminating evidence was put to the accused persons and their statements under Section 313 Cr.P.C. were recorded. Accused Ravi Kumar denied the incriminating circumstances. He also deposed that he is innocent and had been falsely implicated in the present case. Accused stated that the present complaint was filed because his father/co-accused had given complaints against nearby shopkeepers who were indulging in food adulteration. Accused thereafter led defence evidence and examined the following witnesses. DEFENCE EVIDENCE 13. Sh. Rajesh and Sh. Laxmi Narain were examined as DW-1 and DW-2 respectively. Both DW-1 and DW-2 deposed about purchasing grocery items from the shop of the accused persons. They further stated that no other complaint by anyone has been made against accused persons regarding food adulteration. Both witnesses were cross-examined by Ld. SPP for the complainant. 14. Accused Raj Kumar had examined himself as DW-3. He NABEELA NABEELA WALI WALI Date: 2022.10.17 17:10:46 +0530 CC No:- 42902/2016 DA (FSO) v. Ravi Kumar Etc. Page No. 8 of 19 deposed regarding complaints filed by him with the Food Department against sale of adulterated food articles at Lahori Gate. DW-3 stated that due to the complaints and the writ petition which are Mark A (colly) he along with his son have been falsely implicated in the present case. DW-3 was cross- examined by Ld. SPP for the complainant wherein he admitted about a complaint regarding adulteration filed against him. Thereafter, Defence Evidence was closed and final arguments were addressed by both the sides. ARGUMENS 15.
texts.arguments: Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, as all the witnesses have supported the case and there is no contradiction in their testimony. It is submitted that the accused has failed to rebut the findings as given by the PA in his report ExPW1/G. State Of H.P. vs . Lekhraj And Another" (Jt 1999 (9) Sc ... on 17 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135532912/ 5 16. Counsel for the accused on the other hand pointed out contradictions in the testimony of the prosecution witnesses. He argued that PW-2 in his cross-examination has initially denied having knowledge of order of Hon'ble High Court which is Ex.PW2/D1 and thereafter admitted about the same. He also pointed out the contradiction in testimony of PW-3 with respect NABEELA NABEELA WALI CC No:- 42902/2016 DA (FSO) v. Ravi Kumar Etc. WALI Date: 2022.10.17 Page No. 9+0530 17:10:55 of 19 to the quantity of the sample lifted. It was argued by Ld. LAC that no public witness was made and no site plan was prepared by PW-1 and PW-3 has wrongly stated the location of the shop of the accused at ground floor. Ld. Counsel for accused further argued that the price of the sample was not paid as per the selling price mentioned on the sample. He also argued that as per Section 13(2) copy of the report Ex.PW1/G dated 06.07.2009 was belatedly sent to the accused on 26.11.2009, hence hampering the right of the accused to file appeal with RFL against the report of PA. Ld. Counsel for accused relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in M/s Alkem Laboratories Ltd. V. State of Madhya Pradesh and Anr. 18. It is to be understood that the charge framed upon the accused was for violation of provision of Section 2(ia) Sub Clause (a)(b) (c) & (m) of PFA Act and Rule 44(c) of PFA Rules r/w Section 7 of the Act punishable under Section 16(1) (a) of PFA Act 1954 and violation of Section 14 A of PFA Act punishable u/s 16(1c) of PFA Act which are read as under:- NABEELA WALI WALI Date: 2022.10.17 17:11:04 +0530 CC No:- 42902/2016 DA (FSO) v. Ravi Kumar Etc. Page No. 10 of 19 Section 2 In this Act unless the context otherwise requires, ia) "adulterated"-an article of food shall be deemed to be adulterated:- (a) if the article sold by a vendor is not of the nature, substance or quality demanded by the purchaser and is to his prejudice, or is not of the nature, substance or quality which it purports or is represented to be; (b) if the article contains any other substance which affects, or if the article is so processed as to affect, injuriously the nature, substance or quality thereof; (c) if any inferior or cheaper substance has been substituted wholly or in part for the article so as to affect injuriously the nature,substance or quality thereof; (m) if the quality or purity of the article falls below the prescribed standard or its constituents are present in quantities not within the prescribed limits of variability but which does not render it injurious to health; State Of H.P. vs . Sale of certain admixtures prohibited.- Notwithstanding the provisions of rule 43, no person shall either by himself or by any servant or agent, sell (a)............. (b)........... (c) ghee which contains any added matter not exclusively derived from milk fat. Digitally signed by NABEELA NABEELA WALI WALI Date: 2022.10.17 17:11:15 +0530 CC No:- 42902/2016 DA (FSO) v. Ravi Kumar Etc. Page No. 11 of 19 Section 14A. Vendor to disclose the name, etc., of the person from whom the article of food was purchased.- State Of H.P. vs . Lekhraj And Another" (Jt 1999 (9) Sc ... on 17 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135532912/ The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case reported as State of H.P. Vs. Lekhraj and another" (JT 1999 (9) SC 43) , observed as under: "...In the deposition of witnesses there are always normal discrepancy, however, honest and truthful they may be. Such discrepancies are due to normal errors of observations, normal errors of memory due to lapse of time, due to mental disposition such as shock and horror at the time of occurrence, and the like. "... The traditional dogmatic hypertechnical approach has to be replaced by rational, realistic and genuine approach for administering justice in a criminal trial". 22. It is also argued by Ld. Counsel for accused that no person from public was made a witness. However Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ambika Prasad & Anr v. State (2002) (2) Crimes 63 (SC) has held that it is know fact that independent persons are reluctant to be a witness or to assist the NABEELA NABEELA WALI WALI Date: 2022.10.17 17:11:31 +0530 CC No:- 42902/2016 DA (FSO) v. Ravi Kumar Etc. Page No. 13 of 19 investigation. Furthermore "... In Ashraf Ali Vs. State (Delhi) 1991 SCC 203, it has been observed that: "The testimony of a witness is not to be disbelieved or discarded on the ground that the he happens to be an official witness but it is an equally well recognized rule of caution that Court should look for independent corroboration to the testimony of official witness in such cases. Further the relevant provisions under which the copy of PA report is required to be sent to the accused are as under: Section 13 Report of public analyst-(2) On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under section 14A, forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired, either or both of them may make an application to the court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory" NABEELA WALI WALI Date: 2022.10.17 17:11:58 +0530 CC No:- 42902/2016 DA (FSO) v. Ravi Kumar Etc. However as observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in "T.V Usman v. Food Inspector, Tellicherry" (AIR 1994 SC 1818) that mere delay as such will not per se be fatal to the prosecution case even in cases where the sample continues to remain fit for analysis inspite of the delay because the accused is in no way prejudiced on the merits of the case in respect of such delay. Furthermore in view of the observation of Hon'ble Apex Court in "T.V Usman v. Food Inspector, Tellicherry" (AIR 1994 SC 1818) the accused was required to show that the delay resulted in the sample becoming unfit for examination. 34. In P. K. Tejani v. M. r. Dange, (1974) CrLJ 313 (SC), Hon'ble Justice Krishna Iyer observed that, in food offences strict liability is the rule not merely under IPC but all over the world.
